Geometry columns from DuckDB to sf

Source: vignettes/articles/duckdb-to-sf.Rmd
duckdb-to-sf.Rmd

A geometry column often starts in a database, is filtered and sorted somewhere in the middle, and ends in sf for a map or a spatial join. Each hand-off is a chance to lose something: digits when the column travels as text, the coordinate reference system when a reader does not know where to look for it, the meaning of an edge when a line on the sphere is read as a straight one.

This article follows one column from DuckDB to sf and back, with zugeo holding it in between. None of DuckDB, sf or qio is needed by zugeo; the article uses all three.

library(zugeo)
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
invisible(DBI::dbExecute(con, "INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;"))

From DuckDB, as GeoParquet

DuckDB writes a query result as GeoParquet, with the CRS in the file. Here are ten thousand random points over Iberia, in WGS 84 longitude and latitude.

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
invisible(DBI::dbExecute(con, "SELECT setseed(0.42)"))
invisible(DBI::dbExecute(con, sprintf("
  COPY (
    SELECT i AS id,
           ST_SetCRS(ST_Point(-9.5 + random() * 12.5, 36 + random() * 7.8),
                     'OGC:CRS84') AS geometry
    FROM range(10000) t(i)
  ) TO '%s' (FORMAT parquet, GEOPARQUET_VERSION 'BOTH')", path)))

geo_parquet_info() reads the footer and nothing else: the row count, the encoding, the CRS DuckDB stored, and the box from the column’s statistics.

geo_parquet_info(path)
#> <zugeo_parquet_info: 10,000 rows in 1 row groups; GeoParquet 1.0.0>
#> * geometry: WKB GEOMETRY; Point; crs projjson: WGS 84 (CRS84); edges planar; bbox [-9.49522715809373 36.0000097816499, 2.99996306555653 43.7997633161704]

geo_read_parquet() gives a data frame whose geometry column is a geo_vctr, its CRS taken from the file.

df <- geo_read_parquet(path)
head(df, 3)
#>   id                                      geometry
#> 1  0 POINT (-0.1599482076109382 39.44579523739312)
#> 2  1 POINT (-1.0796949709503902 38.57168598702719)
#> 3  2 POINT (-1.9511585203605986 39.79967235830755)
geo_crs(df$geometry)
#> <zugeo_crs projjson: WGS 84 (CRS84)>

In zugeo

The column stays in Arrow memory. Its boxes, Hilbert keys and index are computed over the coordinates. Sorting by Hilbert key puts nearby points next to each other, which is what lets a reader skip a file’s row groups.

df <- df[geo_sort(df$geometry), ]
geo_box_all(df$geometry)
#> <geo_extent[1]; crs projjson: WGS 84 (CRS84); edges planar>
#> [1] [-9.49522715809373 36.0000097816499, 2.99996306555653 43.7997633161704]

A packed R-tree answers “which points fall in this box”, here a box around Lisbon.

tree <- geo_rtree(df$geometry)
lisbon <- geo_extent(-9.5, 38.5, -8.9, 39, crs = geo_crs(df$geometry))
near <- geo_query_box(tree, lisbon)
length(near)
#> [1] 28

To sf

WKB is the bridge: geo_as_wkb() gives a list of raw vectors that sf reads directly, and geo_crs_text() gives the CRS in a form PROJ reads.

pts <- sf::st_sf(
  id = df$id[near],
  geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(
    unclass(geo_as_wkb(df$geometry[near])),
    crs = geo_crs_text(df$geometry)
  )
)
pts[1:3, ]
#> Simple feature collection with 3 features and 1 field
#> Geometry type: POINT
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: -9.472545 ymin: 38.5073 xmax: -9.415429 ymax: 38.55168
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84 (CRS84)
#>     id                   geometry
#> 1 5375 POINT (-9.440974 38.54394)
#> 2  810  POINT (-9.415429 38.5073)
#> 3 8390 POINT (-9.472545 38.55168)
sf::st_crs(pts) == sf::st_crs("OGC:CRS84")
#> [1] TRUE

Nothing was rounded on the way. The coordinates sf holds are the doubles DuckDB wrote, bit for bit.

back <- geo_vctr(sf::st_as_binary(sf::st_geometry(pts)))
identical(geo_coords(back)[c("x", "y")], geo_coords(df$geometry[near])[c("x", "y")])
#> [1] TRUE

And back to GeoParquet

A geometry column from sf comes back the same way, with its CRS given explicitly, and goes out as GeoParquet 2.0. DuckDB reads it and finds the same extent zugeo does.

out <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
again <- data.frame(id = pts$id)
again$geometry <- geo_vctr(sf::st_as_binary(sf::st_geometry(pts)),
  crs = sf::st_crs(pts)$input
)
geo_write_parquet(again, out)
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, sprintf(paste(
  "SELECT count(*) AS n, min(ST_X(geometry)) AS xmin, max(ST_X(geometry)) AS xmax",
  "FROM '%s'"
), out))
#>    n      xmin      xmax
#> 1 28 -9.489615 -8.936077
geo_box_all(again$geometry)
#> <geo_extent[1]; crs projjson: WGS 84 (CRS84); edges planar>
#> [1] [-9.48961521673695 38.5072950083719, -8.93607727962498 38.9574014626128]

Where the guarantees stop

zugeo carries a CRS but does not interpret it: geo_crs_equal() compares two without PROJ, and anything that needs a transformation is sf’s or PROJ’s job. Lines with spherical edges are carried and written as GeoParquet GEOGRAPHY, but a planar box or a planar Hilbert key of them is refused unless asked for with lossy, because it can be wrong. And WKB has no place for an edge type, so geo_as_wkb() on such lines is an error by default: sf would read them as planar.
